# Release Notes - awake 0.7.0-beta

Release date: 2026-10-24
Package: `awake-daemon.win64.zip`

The seventh beta release of **awake**, a Windows command line tool that keeps
the system awake. The headline feature of this release is **timed
keep-awake**: tell the system how long to stay awake and let the tool
release it for you.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This project is generated by AI and has not been extensively reviewed.
> Please scrutinize the code carefully before use. The author is not
> responsible or liable for any consequences arising from the use of this
> software.

## Highlights

- **Timed keep-awake** (`awake 1 for <period>` / `awake 1 until <HH:MM>`):
  enable keep-awake for a limited time and let it expire automatically - no
  need to run `awake 0` afterwards.
  - Periods accept compound units, for example `for 30m`, `for 1h30m`,
    `for 2h`.
  - `until` takes a 24-hour clock time; a time that has already passed
    today rolls over to tomorrow with a warning (`1h7m from now`).
  - Expiry is silent: the daemon simply releases the requirement and keeps
    running.
  - Expiry is measured with a monotonic clock (`GetTickCount64`) on the
    daemon side, so changing the system clock or a DST switch cannot move
    the expiry point, and client and daemon never need to agree on the
  current time.
  - The remaining time is visible in `awake status`
    (`MANUAL_REMAIN`/`SCREEN_REMAIN` protocol fields).
  - `awake screen on for <period>` works the same way for the screen
    keep-awake.
- **Version banner with the build commit**: `awake version` and `awake help`
  now print the git commit the binary was built from, for example
  `awake 0.7.0-beta (git aa41079)`.
- **Automated releases**: GitHub Actions now builds, tests and publishes a
  signed release whenever a version tag is pushed; the tag is checked
  against the version in `CMakeLists.txt` so they can never drift apart.
- **Unit tests**: the shared library (configuration parsing, protocol
  serialization/parsing, time parsing) is covered by a Catch2 test suite
  that runs in CI.
- **First-run experience**: an AI-generated software reminder is printed on
  the error stream on first contact.

## Fixes

- Daemon autostart no longer fails on a fresh Windows profile where the
  `...\CurrentVersion\Run` key does not exist yet - the key is created when
  enabling autostart.

## Compatibility

- The timed form extends the `KEEP_AWAKE` request with an optional seconds
  argument. Old daemons reject the new syntax with a clear error, old
  clients are unaffected. As always, use the client and the daemon from the
  same package.

## Full command list

```
awake help               Show the help message.
awake version            Show the version.
awake aliases            Show every command alias.
awake 0                  Disable keep-awake.
awake 1                  Enable keep-awake (blocks idle sleep/hibernation).
awake 1 for <period>     Enable keep-awake for a limited time, e.g. 30m,
                         1h30m, 2h.
awake 1 until <HH:MM>    Enable keep-awake until that clock time (tomorrow
                         if passed).
awake status             Show daemon, keep-awake, screen, autostart and
                         watch list status.
awake screen on          Keep the screen on (blocks screen off, screensaver
                         and idle lock).
awake screen on for <period>   Keep the screen on for a limited time.
awake screen off         Stop keeping the screen on.
awake daemon on          Start the background daemon.
awake daemon off         Stop the background daemon.
awake daemon enable      Start the daemon automatically at logon.
awake daemon disable     Do not start the daemon automatically at logon.
awake reload             Re-read the configuration file immediately.
awake reset              Reset the configuration file (asks for
                         confirmation).
awake add <imagename>    Add an image name to the watch list.
awake del <imagename>    Remove an image name from the watch list.
```

See `awake aliases` for the shorthand forms of these commands.

## Installation

1. Extract `awake.exe` and `awake.daemon.exe` from this package into any
   folder. Both executables are statically linked and have no runtime
   dependencies.
2. Run `awake daemon on` (or simply `awake 1`) to start using the tool.
   The configuration file `awake.ini` is created next to the executables on
   first use; the first command also asks for the license.
3. Optional: run `awake daemon enable` to start the daemon automatically at
   every logon.

## Notes

- Keep-awake and screen keep-awake states live in the daemon's memory only;
  after a daemon restart they are inactive again (a running timed keep-awake
  expires with it).
- The daemon sends a one-shot stay-awake notification when it starts,
  regardless of the current settings.
- If you enabled autostart and later move the executables to another folder,
  `awake status` will flag the stale entry and `awake daemon enable` in the
  new location fixes it.
- Building from source needs PowerShell 7; set `AWAKE_SDK_ROOT` or use
  `utils\toolchain.ini` when the toolchain is not in a default location.
- This is a beta release; the behaviour and the command line interface may
  still change in incompatible ways before 1.0.
